acquisition.quote: Data were acquired by the TanDEM-X mission between 2011 and 2015.

bucket.credentials: none: anonymous HTTPS GET requests with a Range header; no account, key, token or signature
bucket.url_rule: https://<bucket>.s3.<region>.amazonaws.com/<tile>/<tile>.tif, the S3 virtual-hosted-style URL of s3://<bucket>/<tile>/<tile>.tif

readme_tile_size.quote: GLO-30 Public The properties of COG files specific to this dataset: original height: 3601 pixels COG height: 3600 pixels TIFF tile size: 1024 * 1024 pixels

tiles_touched.definition: the internal COG tiles of band 1 that the pixel window intersects, with the byte offset and size the TIFF tile index states (GDAL TIFF metadata BLOCK_OFFSET and BLOCK_SIZE); held_in_ranges says whether every byte of the tile is in the stored byte ranges. GDAL states no offset or size for a tile the file does not store (a sparse file) or whose tile index entry it cannot read; such a tile has offset, size and held_in_ranges null, and stored_bytes is then null, not a sum over the other tiles

crs.name: WGS 84
crs.stated_by: the COG's GeoTIFF keys, as GDAL reads them

live_probe_budget.note: an observation of this server-side read, not a browser measurement; an over-budget read is recorded as over budget and does not fail the command
live_probe_budget.reader: io.read_remote_cog_window with 262144-byte aligned blocks, so bytes_fetched also holds the header, the block alignment and any other bytes GDAL read; touched_tile_bytes are the touched tiles' sizes as the TIFF tile index states them, null when it states no size for some touched tile
live_probe_budget.rule: PRD 8.7: the first live probe reads at most 4 MB of DEM

nodata.note: the COG declares no nodata value, so only non-finite values are masked

range_read.phase_definition: header: the requests sent before the window's pixels were decoded (the first block, which states the object size, the COG header and the layout); window: the requests sent while the window was decoded
range_read.sha256_note: the tile was not downloaded whole, so its SHA-256 is unknown; local_sha256 is that of the fetched byte ranges held in local_path, at the positions listed in ranges

units.record_units: meters, as the Copernicus DEM collection description states ('Vertical Unit: meters'); the COG states no band units

values.elevation_units: meters, as the Copernicus DEM collection description states ('Vertical Unit: meters'); the COG states no band units

live_probe_quality_rule.rule: PRD 8.7 step 4: a live probe needs a valid fraction of at least 0.8

values.method: quality.validity_mask(window, nodata=the file's nodata) and quality.valid_fraction over the stored values; min and max over valid pixels

vertical_datum.file_note: the COG's CRS has no vertical part, so the file does not state the vertical datum

window.centre_basis: the coordinates the English Wikipedia article 'Holuhraun' states (64.85° N, 16.83° W; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holuhraun, read on 2026-11-14 when this source was written). The pilot does not download that page (Wikipedia answers Python's default HTTP client with HTTP 403), so the centre is a stated choice of the pilot, not an observation; PRD 5 names Holuhraun as the first Earth region
window.definition: the square of side_m metres centred on the centre in the UTM CRS (PRD 5: Earth windows are computed in the local UTM zone with pyproj); its edges, densified to densify_points points each, are transformed to EPSG:4326 and bounded, and the pixel window holds every pixel whose cell, as the COG's geotransform defines it, intersects that bounding box
window.role: the live-probe footprint of PRD 8.7 (a 5 km x 5 km window) at a stated centre; a pilot probe of the read path, not a target or search window
window.utm_zone_rule: the standard 6-degree UTM zone of the centre longitude, north or south by the centre latitude; the Norway and Svalbard exceptions are not applied

description: One window of one Copernicus DEM GLO-30 Public COG read by HTTP range requests from the public AWS bucket, server-side, as fetched by the T1 pilot (PRD 5 row 11; 8.7 live-probe footprint and budget; 9 G0, one Copernicus COG read). Raw observations only: this read sends no Origin header and is not the browser-origin CORS check (T1-07), cop30_mode is chosen by the team at G0, and the shipping mode and the G0 status are a human checkpoint (PRD 23.6).

field_notes.acquisition_time: unknown for this tile: the COG states no acquisition time; acquisition quotes the collection-level statement of the collection description
field_notes.centre: the window centre is a stated pilot choice with its basis in tile_choice; it is not a target window and sets nothing in config/run.yaml
field_notes.crs_and_frame: the horizontal CRS WKT the COG states
field_notes.effective_resolution: unknown: the COG states none and this record derives none (PRD 5 row 11, R16)
field_notes.units: the COG states no band units; the record's units are those the Copernicus DEM collection description states for the vertical axis, else unknown
field_notes.version: the release the AWS registry entry states; the COG states no version, so the release of this tile is not read from the file
field_notes.vertical_datum: read from the file's CRS where it has a vertical part, else unknown for the file; the collection description's statement is quoted beside it

open_g0_items: G0 needs a Copernicus COG read from a browser origin with the CORS result recorded (PRD 9); this read is server-side and sends no Origin header. The Origin-header check is T1-07, and cop30_mode is chosen by the team at G0
The effective support of GLO-30 (PRD 5 row 11, R16) is not established here
No WorldCover or other bare-ground mask is applied (D31)
The G0 status and the shipping mode are a human checkpoint (PRD 23.6)

surface_model_caveat.caveat: Copernicus GLO-30 is a digital surface model: its heights include vegetation, buildings and infrastructure, so terrain statistics from it are not bare-ground statistics unless the window is masked to bare or sparse cover (PRD 5 row 11, D31); no such mask is applied here

quotes.quote: The Copernicus DEM is a Digital Surface Model (DSM) which represents the surface of the Earth including buildings, infrastructure and vegetation.
